sheets.title: Bhakti, Sufi and Sikh traditions
sheets.intro: Alvars to Tyagaraja, Acharyas, Varkaris, Sikh Gurus, Sufi orders.

rows.v: Loving devotion; direct bond with God; no priest needed
South India, 7th – 12th c. (Alvars, Nayanars) vs Jainism, Buddhism; then north
Caste oppression; artisans and low castes drawn; Islam's monotheism, Sufi openness; Advaita too abstract
God with form (Rama, Krishna) – Tulsidas, Surdas, Mirabai, Vallabha; idols, bhajans
Formless God – Kabir, Nanak, Ravidas, Dadu; nam, no idols
Vernacular literature; softer caste walls; Hindu – Muslim mixing
Spiritual, not structural reform – caste survived
63 Shiva saints; Tevaram (Appar, Sambandar, Sundarar); Manikkavachakar – Tiruvasagam; woman Karaikkal Ammaiyar; Sekkilar – Periya Puranam (63 lives)
12 Vishnu saints; Nalayira Divya Prabandham (4,000) compiled by Nathamuni (10th c.); Nammalvar – Tiruvaymoli (greatest); Andal – Tiruppavai (raised by Periyalvar)
Prapatti – full surrender
Tamil
8th c. (788 – 820); born Kaladi, Kerala
Advaita – soul is Brahman; world is Maya
Sringeri (south, Yajur), Puri (east, Rig), Dwarka (west, Sama), Badrinath / Jyotirmath (north, Atharva)
1017 – 1137; seat Srirangam
Vishishtadvaita (qualified non-dualism) – souls distinct but tied to Brahman
Sri Bhashya, Vedartha Sangraha
Srivaishnava
Hoysala Vishnuvardhana turned Vaishnava
12th c.; minister of Kalachuri Bijjala (Kalyana)
Virashaiva / Lingayat – no caste, temples, idols; Ishtalinga worn on body
Short Kannada free verse; Anubhava Mantapa (hall of debate, Allama Prabhu presided)
Basavanna, Allama Prabhu, Akka Mahadevi (woman; Chennamallikarjuna)
Cobbler; father of vachana poetry
Shatsthala (6 stages), Panchacharas (5 conducts)

keys.name: Madhva and Nimbarka

rows.v: 1238 – 1317; Dvaita (soul and God always distinct; world real); Udupi Krishna matha (8 mathas); Panchabheda (5 differences)
Dvaitadvaita; Radha – Krishna
Shankara – Advaita; Ramanuja – Vishishtadvaita; Vallabha – Shuddhadvaita

traps: Nimbarka = Dvaitadvaita; Vallabha = Shuddhadvaita; Madhva = Dvaita

rows.v: Matsyendranath founded; Gorakhnath – hatha yoga
18 Tamil Siddhars – Siddha medicine
Dnyaneshwar came from the Nath line
Vithoba (Vitthal), Pandharpur; pilgrims = Varkaris; Abhangas in Marathi
1275 – 1296; Dnyaneshwari (Gita), Amrutanubhav; guru-brother Nivruttinath
Tailor; verses in Adi Granth
Mahar; against untouchability; wife Soyarabai, sister Nirmala
Gora Kumbhar (potter, Ter); Narhari Sonar (goldsmith); Kanhopatra (courtesan’s daughter)
1448 – 1513; revived Pandharpur temple
1533 – 1599; Bhavarth Ramayana; guru Janardan Swami
17th c.; Dehu; humanist abhangas; disciple Bahina Bai
1608 – 1681; Dasbodh, Manache Shlok; Shivaji's guide
14th – 15th c.; Rama bhakti in Hindi; pupils of all castes – Kabir, Ravidas, Sena, Dhanna, Pipa – bridge south to north
15th c.; raised by weavers Neema and Niru, Varanasi; Nirguna; attacked idols, caste, rituals; dohas; ulatbansi (upside-down sayings); Bijak, Kabir Granthavali; verses in Adi Granth
Leather worker; in Guru Granth; guru of Mirabai (trad.)
1544 – 1603; Dadu Panth (Rajasthan)
1469 – 1539; Talwandi (Nankana Sahib); enlightened at Sultanpur 1496; settled at Kartarpur
Nirguna; one God; against caste, idols
Langar; Nam Japna, Kirat Karna, Vand Chhakna

keys.name: Sikh Gurus 2 – 10

rows.v: 1539 – 52; Gurmukhi; Mall Akhara
1552 – 74; 22 manjis; against sati, purdah; got Akbar to drop the pilgrim tax
1574 – 81; Ramdaspur (Amritsar); Anand Karaj
1581 – 1606; Adi Granth 1604; Harmandir Sahib; executed by Jahangir – first martyr
1606 – 44; Miri – Piri (two swords); Akal Takht
1644 – 61; sheltered Dara Shikoh
1661 – 64; child Guru; Bangla Sahib
1665 – 75; beheaded by Aurangzeb – Sis Ganj; defended Kashmiri Pandits
1675 – 1708; born Patna; Khalsa 1699 (Anandpur); five Ks (kesh, kangha, kara, kachera, kirpan); final Granth at Damdama; Granth as eternal Guru; died Nanded (Hazur Sahib)

traps: Akal Takht – Hargobind; Khalsa – Gobind Singh; Amritsar – Ramdas

keys.name: Krishna and Rama bhakti in the north and east

rows.v: 1479 – 1531; Telugu family; Shuddhadvaita; Pushtimarga (path of grace)
1483 – 1563; Sursagar; Vallabha's disciple
16th c.; Mewar princess; Krishna bhajans
1532 – 1623; Ramcharitmanas (Awadhi); Ramleela; Sankatmochan temple
1486 – 1534; Bengal; Gaudiya Vaishnavism; sankirtan; Puri
1449 – 1568; Assam; Ekasarana Dharma; namghars, sattras, Borgeet, Ankiya Naat
1408 – 1503; Tallapaka; about 32,000 sankirtanas to Venkateswara (sringara and adhyatma); on copper plates; "Pada Kavita Pitamaha"
c. 1450 – 1510; Andhra Mahabhagavatamu; gave it to God, not a king
17th c.; Vemana Satakam (ataveladi metre); against caste, rituals; "Viswadabhirama Vinura Vema"
17th c.; Movva; padams to Muvva Gopala
Kancherla Gopanna; rebuilt Bhadrachalam temple; jailed by Abul Hasan Tana Shah
Krishna Leela Tarangini
Shaped Kuchipudi; Bhama Kalapam
1730 – 1817; woman poet of Tirumala
1767 – 1847; Tiruvaiyaru; Carnatic trinity (with Dikshitar, Syama Sastri); Pancharatna kritis
Islamic mysticism; love of God through a master
Pir / Murshid (master), Murid (pupil), Khalifa (chosen successor)
Khanqah (hospice, free food); Dargah (tomb shrine); Urs (death anniversary); Ziyarat (pilgrimage)
Sama (music, qawwali), Zikr (repeating God's name), Tauba (repentance), Hal (ecstasy), Fanaa (merging in God), Maqamat (stages)
Silsilah (chain)
Wahdat-ul-Wujud – Ibn-i-Arabi (unity of being); Wahdat-ul-Shuhud – Sirhindi (unity of appearance)
Biddat (innovation); Amrita Kunda (yoga text) into Arabic, Persian
Khwaja Muinuddin Chishti, Ajmer, after 1192
Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki (Delhi, Mehrauli) → Baba Farid Ganj-i-Shakar (Pakpattan; Punjabi verse in Adi Granth) → Nizamuddin Auliya (Delhi; saw 7 Sultans) → Nasiruddin Chiragh-i-Delhi
Hamiduddin Nagauri (Hindawi); Salim Chishti (Sikri; Jahangir named for him); Gesu Daraz (Gulbarga)
Love, simple life, no state posts, sama allowed
Amir Khusrau (Nizamuddin)

Bihar; Suhrawardi branch; Sharfuddin Yahya Maneri
